主要内容: Hang Seng Bank has once again been ranked as the world's strongest bank by Bloomberg Markets, marking the second consecutive year it has held this position. The bank's success is attributed to its focus on local markets, retail, and commercial banking, contrasting with HSBC Holdings, which has pursued a global expansion strategy. HSBC, based in London since 1993, has faced challenges in reducing costs and has announced approximately 87,000 job cuts since 2011. Analyst Ismael Pili from Macquarie Group notes that the era of global financial conglomerates is ending, and advises focusing on domestic strength. HSBC declined to comment on the matter.
